comments.content:
FROM CHILD 2 (task-8145137c, goal-close readiness) — what your UI/docs/live-drive assertions can rely on, and ONE wall you will hit.

1) THE OFFER RULE, exactly as shipped (apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.ts:151-166). For an EXECUTION_ENABLED or CLOSING goal the ladder now calls `input.closeReadiness(goalId)` and returns `[goal.close, repository.publish]` only when the kind is NO_CONTRACT or READY; NOT_READY and UNREADABLE return `[repository.publish]` alone (fail closed). COMPLETED still returns publish only. The fact is consulted for NO other lifecycle (spy-asserted zero calls for DRAFT/COMPLETED/compiler-lane goals), and it is composed lazily in affordance-read.ts:266-271 from `goalCloseReadinessFor(store, projectId, goalId).kind` — read fresh on every poll, never cached, so an acceptance landing between two polls shows up on the next one.

2) THE FOUR KINDS (apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-close-readiness.ts): NO_CONTRACT (coverage refuses DOCUMENT_COVERAGE_READ_GOAL_UNBOUND, or the view carries zero contracts / zero criteria) | READY {criteria} | NOT_READY {criteria, verified} | UNREADABLE {code, layer}. CONTRACT-LESS GOALS ARE UNCHANGED — the seed/Foundation journey is NO_CONTRACT, so its goal.close card still appears right after activation (board-chain.spec.ts:392 verified green: `ok 1 [chromium] ... an operator can click the whole bootstrap chain from an empty store (21.6s)`).

3) THERE IS NO DETAIL STRING ON THE WIRE — do not assert one. The refusal is `GOAL_CLOSE_CRITERIA_UNVERIFIED` + layer `DAEMON_PREREQUISITE`, code+layer only, exactly like its 8 roster siblings. Measured why: `ServiceRefused` (bootstrap-ledger.ts:125-133) has no message field, only `error: RuntimeError | null`, and `RuntimeError.code` must be a REGISTERED `RuntimeErrorCode` — `createRuntimeError` fails an unregistered code closed to UNKNOWN_ERROR with details STRIPPED (runtime-error-factory.ts:93-103), which is strictly worse than the code itself. The counts (`criteria`, `verified`) live on the readiness value and on the coverage read the screen already shows. needs-you-model.ts:110-135 needs no production change: it derives READY_TO_CLOSE from coverage totals + the presence of the offer, and both now move together.

4) THE WALL, measured, not inferred — A PRD-COMPILED CONTRACT-BEARING GOAL STILL CANNOT CLOSE, for a reason neither this row nor child 1 owns. `runApprovalIntentCommand` (`approval.decide_intent`, the compiled/PRD journey) writes `GoalExecutionEnabled.approval.approvedNodeScope: []` — read verbatim from the committed event bytes. `readApprovedNodeScope` (goal-close-prerequisite.ts:75) requires a NON-EMPTY scope, so `qualifyGoalClosure` refuses `GOAL_CLOSE_REVIEW_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` ("no current approval names an approved node scope") regardless of coverage. Every other approval field is correct (decision APPROVE, lifecycle DECIDED, validity CURRENT). My arm at goal-close-readiness.test.ts:418 pins exactly that hand-off: once readiness is READY the close stops refusing on MY code and refuses on that one instead. The `approval.decide` path DOES write a scope, so the contract-LESS journey closes end to end today (arm :451, full authenticated wire, GoalCompleted x1). No board row owns the empty-scope gap (I grepped every .moe/tasks row naming approvedNodeScope + decide_intent: only DONE rows). If your live drive is a contract-bearing goal, plan for that row first or your journey stops one gate past mine.

5) COST, measured on this machine (temporary probe, removed; restore proven by blob hash == HEAD): a `/affordances/read` surface read on a contract-bearing world 54-65 ms, of which the new coverage read is 27-59 ms per enabled/closing goal; a contract-less (seed) goal pays 9.1 ms of a 35.7 ms surface read. Linear per offered goal — three contract-bearing goals add roughly 81-178 ms per poll. Follow-up worth folding into the epic-final hardening row, not a new row: `createDocumentCoverageReadPort` re-reads the durable ledger per goal, while affordance-read.ts has already read it once per surface read.
